claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I'm asking about my daughter Alex. She's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're asking about your daughter Alex, who is 8 years old.

Let me ask you a few questions to determine your eligibility:

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I need to understand your relationship with Alex:

**Do you live with Alex, or if she doesn't live with you, are you paying at least the equivalent of the Child Benefit amount towards her upkeep (such as for food, clothes, or pocket money)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: She doesn't live with me, but I do help out with her upkeep - I contribute about £10 a week towards things she needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. To assess whether your contributions are sufficient, I need to understand a bit more:

**Is Alex living with someone else who is currently claiming Child Benefit for her (such as her other parent or another family member)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, no one else is claiming Child Benefit for her.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. That's helpful to know. Let me ask about your contributions:

**You mentioned you contribute £10 per week towards Alex's upkeep. Can you tell me what these contributions cover - for example, are they for food, clothes, pocket money, or other needs? Also, are you making these contributions regularly every week?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I make the contributions regularly every week. I help out with things like clothes for her and money for school dinners - just the basics she needs really.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. I have one more important question:

**Do you or your partner (if you have one) have an individual income over £60,000 per year?**

(This won't affect whether you can *get* Child Benefit, but it may mean you have to pay a tax charge on it.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'd rather not get into my income details right now - I'm mainly just trying to figure out if I'm eligible to claim at all first.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's absolutely fine - I understand. Let me assess your eligibility based on the information you've provided.

To clarify one final point before I give you my assessment:

**Who does Alex live with currently, and do you know if that person or household receives any support from the local council for Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: She's been in local authority care - she's been there for a couple of months now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for sharing that important information. I need to understand this situation a bit better:

**Has Alex been in local authority care for more than 8 weeks? And during this time, do you know if she spends any regular time at home with you - for example, at least 24 hours a week, or perhaps 2 nights in a row each week?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: She's been there for about 12 weeks now, and no, she doesn't come home to stay with me - she's at the care home full-time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me carefully consider the rules based on your situation:

- Alex is 8 years old (under 16, so age requirement is met)
- You live in the UK
- Alex does not live with you
- You contribute £10 per week towards her upkeep (for clothes and school dinners)
- No one else is currently claiming Child Benefit for her
- Alex has been in local authority care for 12 weeks (more than 8 weeks)

According to the Child Benefit rules, when a child goes into care for more than 8 weeks, the parent or carer usually stops being entitled to Child Benefit. There is an exception if the child spends at least 24 hours a week at home, but you've confirmed that Alex is at the care home full-time and doesn't come home to stay with you.

While you are making regular contributions to Alex's upkeep, the fact that she has been in local authority care for more than 8 weeks and is not spending regular time at home with you means you would not qualify for Child Benefit under the current rules.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to inform you that based on your circumstances, you would be **ineligible** for Child Benefit for Alex.

The key issue is that Alex has been in local authority care for 12 weeks, which is more than the 8-week threshold set by the rules. After 8 weeks in care, parents typically lose entitlement to Child Benefit unless the child spends at least 24 hours a week at home with them. Since Alex is at the care home full-time and doesn't come home to stay with you regularly, this exception doesn't apply.

I understand this may not be the answer you were hoping for. If Alex's circumstances change in the future - for example, if she starts spending regular time at home with you (such as 2 nights in a row each week or 7 days or more in a row) - you may be able to claim Child Benefit at that point. If that happens, you should contact HMRC to discuss your eligibility.

However, Alex has been in local authority care for 12 weeks, which exceeds the 8-week threshold. According to the rules, when a child goes into care for more than 8 weeks, the parent is no longer entitled to Child Benefit. The exception to this rule is if the child spends at least 24 hours a week at home, but the claimant confirmed that Alex is at the care home full-time and does not come home to stay. While the claimant does contribute £10 per week towards Alex's upkeep, this does not override the 8-week care rule when the child is not spending regular time at home. Therefore, the claimant is ineligible for Child Benefit for Alex.
